# Explainer Studio

> Explainer Studio turns a topic string into a narrated, animated educational explainer
> video (MP4). It ships as one PyPI package, `explainer-studio`, with a typer CLI
> (`explainer`) and a library API (`from explainer import Pipeline, Script`). A four-stage
> deterministic pipeline does the work: an LLM writes a schema-validated script, a TTS
> provider narrates each scene, headless Chromium renders animated frames from
> self-contained HTML templates, and FFmpeg composes the MP4. The defaults need no API
> keys (heuristic LLM + edge-tts). It renders vector/HTML scenes, NOT photoreal footage.

Key facts for integration:
- Install: `pip install explainer-studio` then `playwright install chromium`; FFmpeg and
  ffprobe must be on PATH. `explainer doctor` verifies all three.
- CLI: `explainer generate "<topic>" [--lang --audience --duration --fps --res --llm
  --tts --voice --music --script --keep-artifacts -o]`, plus `doctor`, `init`, `voices`,
  `templates list`, `templates preview <kind>`.
- Library: `Pipeline(llm=None, tts="edge", voice=None, on_progress=None)`;
  `.generate(topic, ...)` runs all four stages, `.render(script, ...)` skips scripting.
  Both return `GenerateResult(mp4_path, script, work_dir)`.
- A `Script` has 3–6 `Scene`s; the first must be kind `title` and the last `takeaway`.
  Scene kinds: title, concept, steps, compare, chart, takeaway, animation. Each scene's
  `data` is validated against its template's JSON Schema before rendering.
- Audio-first timing is a hard invariant: scene duration = narration audio duration +
  0.4 s tail pad. Narration length defines scene length, never the reverse.
- Determinism: `window.renderFrame(t)` must be a pure function of t (0→1). No `Date.now()`,
  no `requestAnimationFrame`, no unseeded randomness. Same inputs produce a
  pixel-identical video.
- For the six fixed templates the LLM only fills schema-validated data, which is sanitized
  (HTML tags, on*= handlers, javascript:/data: URIs stripped) before injection. The
  `animation` kind additionally lets the model author markup/css/js executed as draw(t);
  those fields skip tag-stripping but are rejected if they contain Date, Math.random,
  timers, fetch/XHR or external URLs.
- Rendering is sandboxed: every non-`file://` request is blocked in Chromium, and the
  template registry rejects any `index.html` with external `src=`/`href=` URLs.
- Config precedence: CLI args > `EXPLAINER_*` env vars > `~/.explainer/config.toml` >
  defaults. Missing provider API keys fail fast at startup.
- Extend via entry points: group `explainer.templates` (each resolving to a `get_path()`
  returning a directory with `template.json` + `index.html`) and group
  `explainer.providers` (names prefixed `llm_` / `tts_`).

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/README.md):
  full overview — quickstart, CLI and Python API reference, template contract, providers,
  determinism guarantees
- [Quickstart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/docs/quickstart.md):
  install through first generated video, step by step
- [CLI reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/docs/cli.md):
  every command, option, and stage-specific exit code
- [Python API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/docs/api.md):
  Pipeline, Script, Scene, GenerateResult, ProgressEvent
- [Template system](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/docs/templates.md):
  the setSceneData/renderFrame contract and how to author a custom template
- [Providers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/docs/providers.md):
  LLM and TTS adapters, configuration, and writing your own
- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/AGENTS.md):
  repo layout, commands, and invariants for coding agents
- [CONTRIBUTING](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/CONTRIBUTING.md):
  development setup, testing strategy, and review expectations

## Source (canonical references)

- [Pipeline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/explainer/core/pipeline.py):
  the four-stage orchestrator, timing invariant, and progress events
- [Schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/explainer/core/schema.py):
  Script/Scene/SceneKind pydantic models and template-schema validation
- [Renderer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/explainer/core/renderer.py):
  parallel headless-Chromium frame capture and network blocking
- [Composer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/explainer/core/composer.py):
  FFmpeg segment encoding, crossfade transitions, and music ducking
- [Registry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/explainer/core/registry.py):
  template discovery order and self-containment checks
- [Sanitizer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/explainer/core/sanitize.py):
  what is stripped from untrusted LLM scene data
- [Config](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/explainer/config.py):
  resolution order and the full env var / API key mapping
- [Provider protocols](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/explainer/providers/llm_base.py):
  the LLMProvider interface (see `tts_base.py` for TTSProvider)

## Examples

- [Basic usage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/examples/basic_usage.py):
  generating a video from Python with a progress callback
- [Example script JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/examples/photosynthesis_script.json):
  a complete hand-editable Script, usable with `--script`
- [Golden script fixture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/tests/fixtures/golden_script.json):
  the script the snapshot and determinism tests render
- [.env.example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pramodthe/explainer-studio/main/.env.example):
  every environment variable the package reads
